D.treatment: data-driven assessment tools integrated into laparoscopic skills training

O.outcome_detail: number of surgical residents trained and assessed

cells.quote: A total of 2618 surgical residents, median 27 (range 6 - 914), were trained and assessed by data-driven assessment tools for laparoscopic skills training (Table 1).
cells.note: The systematic review reports a descriptive pooled count without a comparative treatment effect.

cells.quote: Residents with the placenta model performed better; the placenta model required more extended time to complete the task; the placenta model was more effective in simulating sylvian fissure splitting, bipolar coagulation of oozing micro vessels, and aneurysm neck and dome dissection; the cadaver model was superior for the simulation of intraoperative rupture and reproduction of real anatomy
cells.note: Qualitative finding from one included comparative study; no quantitative effect size was reported.

cells.quote: No differences were found in surgical outcomes, complications, and duration between two groups; a high degree of appreciation was shown by participants concerning simulator rehearsal; junior neurosurgeons improved their performance with the simulator after a debriefing session
cells.note: The review reports no significant difference but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power.

cells.quote: The mean values of the number of clip attempts, total operative time, ratio of clip attempts to clips used, and time per clip attempt were lower in the VR group (only time per clip was statistically significant)
cells.note: The review reports a statistically significant reduction only for time per clip; no numerical effect size is given.

cells.quote: Trainees succeeded in performing the simulation in line with actual surgery; trainees’ skills improved upon completion of the training with the model
cells.note: Pre-post finding from one included study; no quantitative effect size was reported.
